problem.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $BC = AC$ and $\angle ACB = 40^{\circ}$. Construct the circle with diameter $\overline{BC}$, and let $D$ and $E$ be the other intersection points of the circle with the sides $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{AB}$, respectively. Let $F$ be the intersection of the diagonals of the quadrilateral $BCDE$. What is the degree measure of $\angle BFC$?

steps.title: Where to start: a diameter gives right angles
steps.body: The clue is "circle with diameter $\overline{BC}$". An inscribed angle is half of the arc it cuts off, and a diameter cuts off a semicircle of $180^\circ$. So any point on the circle sees $BC$ at a right angle. Draw the picture: $C$ at the top, $B$ and $A$ at the bottom, with $D$ on $AC$ and $E$ on $AB$.

your_turn.prompt: Which two angles with vertices at $D$ and $E$ must be $90^\circ$?
your_turn.answer: $\angle BDC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle BEC = 90^\circ$, since both cut off the semicircle $BC$.

steps.title: Find the base angles
steps.body: Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $BC = AC$, so the angles at $A$ and $B$ (opposite those equal sides) are equal.

steps.title: Look at triangle $BFC$
steps.body: The diagonals of $BCDE$ are $CE$ and $BD$, and they meet at $F$. So in triangle $BFC$, the angle at $C$ is $\angle ECB$ and the angle at $B$ is $\angle DBC$. Each of these sits in one of the right triangles from Step 1.

your_turn.prompt: Use right triangle $CEB$ (right angle at $E$) to find $\angle ECB$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: In right triangle $CDB$ (right angle at $D$), $\angle DCB = 40^\circ$, so $\angle DBC = 180 - 90 - 40 = 50^\circ$. Careful: this angle is $\angle DBC$, not the base angle $\angle ABC = 70^\circ$, because $BD$ is a different segment from $BA$. Then $\angle BFC = 180 - 20 - 50 = 110^\circ$. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from using the base angle $\angle ABC = 70^\circ$ as the angle of triangle $BFC$ at $B$: $180 - 20 - 70 = 90$. But $F$ lies on $BD$, not on $BA$, so the angle at $B$ is $\angle DBC = 50^\circ$.
